newsitem.title: INDIA: India's lower house approves appropriation bill.
newsitem.headline: India's lower house approves appropriation bill.

text.p: India's lower house of the parliament on Monday approved a bill which appropriates money to all ministries and departments of the central government for 1996/97 (April-March), parliamentary officials said.
The finance bill, which contains the tax proposals in the budget, is expected to be voted and approved before the scheduled adjournment of parliament on Friday, September 13.
Domestic stock markets expect Finance Minister P.Chidambaram to announce changes in a proposed minimum alternate tax (MAT) on high-growth companies in his speech.
But Chidambaram, speaking in the upper house on Monday, gave little indication of making changes in the MAT.
"I don't know why the corporate sector should cry hoarse over this taxation," the Press Trust of India quoted Chidambaram as saying.

"The corporate sector has to pay only 12.9 per cent as tax on the book profits while individuals earning over 10,000 rupees pay as high as 40 per cent tax. In fact, the corporate sector pays on an average an effective taxation rate of only 19 per cent," Chidambaram said.

The finance minister said the government hoped to get $1.5 billion from foreign financial institutions, $3.0 billion from foreign direct investment and $1.5 billion through global depository receipts in 1996/97.
